title: Israel's Secret Iraq Desert Base Exposed Amid Iran War
excerpt: The Wall Street Journal reveals Israel ran a clandestine forward outpost in Iraq's Najaf desert to support its air campaign against Tehran.
body:
Israel secretly built and operated a military base inside Iraq's Najaf desert to fuel its air campaign against Iran — and struck Iraqi soldiers to keep it hidden, according to a bombshell Wall Street Journal report confirmed by two Iraqi security officials on Sunday.

**What happened — a Saddam-era runway, reactivated:**
Israeli forces established a makeshift base using an old airstrip in Iraq's desert during the war against Iran. Early in the war, ignited by joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28, the troops were detected in the Najaf desert and clashed with Iraqi forces, killing one soldier and wounding two others. The military site sits in the Himyar Valley, about 180 kilometers west of the Iraqi city of Najaf, near the border with Saudi Arabia. Israel built the base shortly before the US-Israeli strikes on Iran started, to serve as a logistical hub for the Israeli Air Force — and it also housed special forces troops and search-and-rescue teams poised to act if any Israeli pilots were downed.

**The cover nearly blown — a shepherd, a convoy, an airstrike:**
Iraqi forces nearly discovered the secret site in early March after a local shepherd reported unusual military activity and heavy helicopter traffic. The Iraqi army dispatched troops to investigate, but Israel launched airstrikes to deter them, resulting in the death of one Iraqi soldier and injuries to two others. An Iraqi security official told AFP there were 'indications that the operation involved an Israeli technical team under American military protection,' and confirmed that CH-57 Chinook helicopters were seen on the site. The United States told Iraq to keep its forces away from the Najaf desert for security reasons while Israel operated the outpost.

**What to watch — Baghdad demands answers:**
Iraq's parliament is set to summon the defence and interior ministers following the revelations, with a parliamentary official saying senior security figures would also be questioned. The report arrives as Baghdad faces US pressure to disarm Iran-backed militias, and reports of a foreign force undermining Iraqi sovereignty will stoke serious controversy in the new government.

sources.label: Wall Street Journal (via Times of Israel)

nri_angle: With the US-Israeli war against Iran having already rattled oil markets, energy corridors, and Indian diaspora remittance routes through the Gulf, this revelation of covert Israeli operations inside Iraq raises the stakes for regional stability that directly affects Indian-American families with ties to the Gulf.
